answer: About 706 people survived out of roughly 2,224–2,240 on board, so more than 1,500 died [1][2]. Sources don't agree on the exact number. You'll see figures between about 706 and 712 depending on which passenger and crew records are used and how some people are counted [2][3]. Using the 706 figure, 492 survivors were passengers and 214 were crew [2]. Class made a big difference. About 3 in 5 first-class passengers survived, compared with about 1 in 4 in third class [2]. All the survivors were picked up from the lifeboats by RMS Carpathia.
